name: Ecoline Exim Limited
sector: Cotton and jute export bags; emerging polyester backpacks
summary:
Ecoline Exim is a cotton and jute export-bag manufacturer with useful repeat relationships, newer leased capacity and an emerging domestic backpack line. The investment thesis is an execution-led manufacturing expansion, not demonstrated high-quality compounding. Audited FY26 revenue was ₹278.40 crore, below the FY23 ₹303.66 crore peak; FY26 profit growth also depended on other income while normalized core EBIT declined. The Ahmedabad project offers backward-integration potential, but its ₹65.10 crore original cost and ₹15.10 crore internal-funding requirement matter as much as the ₹50 crore IPO allocation. [S1,S2,S6,S7]

At the last observed NSE close of ₹190.15 on 16 October 2026, the linked base case returns 6.64% annually over five years against a 15% hurdle, despite recovering growth and margins. BQS is 4.52, GQS 3.60 and conditional IAS 3.33, displayed 4.5/3.6/3.3. Classification: Weak setup / value-trap risk. Neither an actual default nor a governance failure is established. Better commissioned-asset returns, sustained collections and a materially lower entry price would change the assessment; a broad sustainability theme alone would not.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Ecoline Exim is a cotton and jute export-bag manufacturer with useful repeat relationships, newer leased capacity and an emerging domestic backpack line. The investment thesis is an execution-led manufacturing expansion, not demonstrated high-quality compounding. Audited FY26 revenue was ₹278.40 crore, below the FY23 ₹303.66 crore peak; FY26 profit growth also depended on other income while normalized core EBIT declined. The Ahmedabad project offers backward-integration potential, but its ₹65.10 crore original cost and ₹15.10 crore internal-funding requirement matter as much as the ₹50 crore IPO allocation. [S1,S2,S6,S7]

At the last observed NSE close of ₹190.15 on 16 October 2026, the linked base case returns 6.64% annually over five years against a 15% hurdle, despite recovering growth and margins. BQS is 4.52, GQS 3.60 and conditional IAS 3.33, displayed 4.5/3.6/3.3. Classification: Weak setup / value-trap risk. Neither an actual default nor a governance failure is established. Better commissioned-asset returns, sustained collections and a materially lower entry price would change the assessment; a broad sustainability theme alone would not.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Ecoline Exim Limited, NSE Emerge ECOLINE, ISIN INE0VBS01016, listed 30 September 2025. Cutoff 20 October 2026; the last market session was 19 October but the last retrieved company trade was 16 October. Price ₹190.15 on 20,515,376 issued shares implies ₹390.10 crore equity value. The audited current scope is standalone, with no current subsidiary, associate or joint venture. Earlier equity-method associates and their residual minority investments are distinguished. Amounts are INR crore unless stated. The horizon is five years, nominal pretax equity hurdle 15%, and the liquidity illustration is ₹5 lakh, not a proposed allocation. [S1,S2,S15]

G1 integrity: Conditional, not failed. Unmodified financial and control opinions coexist with substantial related-party property economics. G2 reliability: Conditional, not an IAS hold. The detailed advances columns and old cash-flow classifications need care, but the current signed balance-sheet subtotal is verified and every claim is explicitly funded or conservatively excluded. G3 survival: Conditional. A credible 15%-sales-down/75-day-collection bear is funded; a stronger 20%/90-day halted-expansion case survives only after dispensing with the assumed ₹3 crore cash buffer. Remote/full-recall and more severe collection cases fail. Hypothetical rescue is never the basis for this gate. G4 tradability: Conditional, not suspended: the eligible SM series has actual trades, but concentration and lot-size risk remain. [S1,S4,S6,S15,S16]

Confidence is High for current signed aggregate P&L, shares and balance-sheet amounts; Medium for economic growth decomposition, normalized profits, cash classification, stewardship and incremental returns; Medium for conditional valuation and coarse historical liquidity, Low for live execution. Forecast uncertainty is high and separate from historical source confidence. No historical factor reaches 9–10.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 2, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 4. BQS = 20%×5 + 20%×5 + 12%×2 + 10%×6 + 12%×4 + 10%×4 + 8%×5 + 8%×5 = 4.52. GQS = 40%×2 + 20%×6 + 15%×4 + 15%×4 + 10%×4 = 3.60. There is no governance, funding or growth-quality override: every aggregate has 100% factor coverage and raw equals final. CASH 4 is a material concern, not a mechanical persistent-poor-cash score of 3 or below.

IAS reuses unrounded BQS once: 25%×4.52 + 35%×2 + 20%×3 + 10%×3 + 10%×6 = 3.33. R 2 follows the exact return-spread schedule: base IRR 6.64% less the 15% hurdle equals approximately −8.36 percentage points. D 3 reflects funded-bear loss and thin survival cash; P 3 reflects improvement required beyond recent growth; L 6 combines observed turnover with implementation risk. REV begins at 1 from negative three-year revenue growth and receives one documented realization adjustment to 2, not a bonus for future capacity. Each factor has its own evidence IDs. Forecast aspirations do not alter demonstrated business scores.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The company converts cotton and jute fabrics into reusable promotional, retail and packaging bags, with cutting, printing, stitching and packing spread across West Bengal and Gujarat. The annual report describes five operating factories and 317,500 sqft, including the newer Badu Unit 2 and leased Taki Road capacity. Ahmedabad expansion funded by the IPO is a different project from this existing operating footprint. Sales are substantially export-led, while the polyester-backpack initiative introduces a domestic institutional customer and different materials/end markets. [S1,S2,S19]

FY26 product sales of₹265.87 crore comprised conventional cotton 54.82%, recycled 12.34%, organic 3.09%, Fairtrade 5.79%, jute 21.04% and others 2.91%, subject to rounding. These percentages use product sales, not total audited operating revenue ₹278.40 crore; export benefits and other operating components explain why the denominators must not be mixed. Conventional cotton's share rose while organic/Fairtrade shares fell, so an unqualified premium-product-mix thesis is unsupported. Management reported 36,000 backpacks delivered in FY26, 60,000 confirmed by 30 April and ₹95 crore export orders, with usual short execution visibility rather than a multi-year guaranteed annuity. [S1,S9]

Cash economics depend on cotton/jute purchase prices, cutting and labor utilization, subcontracting, export freight, exchange rates, trade-credit collection and fabric/WIP inventory. A repeat order does not eliminate shipment delay or price renegotiation; raw-material deflation can reduce reported value even when units recover. Revenue recognition and export shipping cutoff are therefore consequential to both profit and working capital.

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is execution capability: established export relationships, multiple production locations, certification access and the ability to offer several fabric/printing formats. Management reports 70–80% repeat customers and 35-plus countries, but no disclosed contractual lock-in or verified share trend establishes a structural moat. Capacity-stage totals cannot simply be added together as independent finished-bag output. The IPO's engineer-certified estimates themselves depend on operating-day and productivity assumptions. [S1,S2,S10]

FY25 the largest buyer represented 10.75%, top five 38.61% and top ten 57.80% of product sales; the largest-buyer figure was 26.07% in FY24. This is an improvement in concentration, not proof of bargaining power. Top-ten supplier concentration reached 72.12% versus 59.46% in FY24. Domestic backpacks initially depend on one buyer. Competing exporters and substitutable fabrics constrain pricing, while customers can retain Ecoline yet negotiate lower realizations. [S2,S6]

The prospectus does not identify a directly comparable listed pure-play cotton/jute-bag peer. Industrial plastic/sack packaging, textile yarn and branded luggage have materially different product economics and should not lend automatic P/E multiples here. The valuation therefore uses explicit operating-return and financing scenarios, not a generic packaging-sector premium. MOAT5 recognizes useful but contestable processes and relationships.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue FY21–26 was ₹121.58/198.44/303.66/272.19/269.29/278.40 crore. The five-year CAGR is 18.02%, four-year FY22–26 is 8.83%, and the selected mature FY23–26 window is −2.85%. FY21 is a pandemic-affected base, so its recovery is not treated as persistent 18% underlying expansion. Annual additions from FY22 onward were ₹76.85,+105.22,−31.47,−2.90 and +9.11 crore. The comparison policy is disclosed before using the score, not chosen to favor a conclusion. [S1–S3]

Acuité attributes the recent value decline to lower realization. IPO packaging-stage production increased from 62.447 million pieces in FY23 to 65.029 million in FY25, around 2.05% annualized, while cutting grew only modestly and stitching declined. These are different process stages, affected by outsourcing/reconstruction, not a clean sold-volume series. They corroborate a price-related distortion but do not prove strong organic volume expansion. Starting REV 1 therefore receives the permitted single-point adjustment to 2, with no further uplift. FY26 comparable revenue growth was 3.38%; the two halves were ₹139.2244 and ₹139.1753 crore, not an accelerating run rate. [S2,S4,S6]

Revenue is not inflated by line-by-line associate consolidation: FY23/FY24 associates were accounted for by the equity method, adding profit rather than sales. Reported ₹286.88 crore in the FY26 release is total income, not operating revenue; the difference ₹8.483 crore must remain separate. No quantified acquisition-growth contribution or verified FY26 sold-unit bridge is assumed.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The Ahmedabad plan has an original ₹65.1035 crore building, electrical and machinery budget, including quoted taxes: ₹50 crore from the IPO and ₹15.1035 crore internally funded. Land is separately evidenced, with ₹9.9 crore advances already on the books and ₹1.5709 crore remaining capital commitments modeled once. June monitoring showed only ₹0.20 crore project use. Existing March CWIP of ₹11.8613 crore is not silently subtracted from the new project budget: the new office and other works are distinct from Ahmedabad's monitored spending. [S1,S2,S7]

Base and bull spend the remaining ₹64.9035 crore over two years; bear spends it over four. Authorization-specific escrow funds the first ₹49.8 crore, not unrelated dividends or debt. Base revenue growth is 6%, 10%, 10%, 8%, 8%, with core EBITDA margins of 8%, 9.5%, 10.5%, 11%, 11%, compared with FY26 no-FX EBITDA margin of 8.57%. These are analyst assumptions for utilization and integration, not company guidance. Bull requires 10–16% growth and a 13% terminal margin. Bear delays commissioning and sustains weaker margins. Maintenance, replacement working capital, land, capital creditors, tax and actual demand borrowing are funded before equity is valued.

A current operating-capital proxy is ₹136.41 crore: net operating working capital ₹88.0451 crore, productive PPE/CWIP/capital advances ₹23.7245 crore, land ₹9.9 crore and rental deposits ₹14.7396 crore. FY26 no-FX EBIT taxed at 26% yields ₹15.65 crore NOPAT, about 11.47% on that year-end proxy, not a true incremental ROIC. It does not clearly exceed a reasoned 12–15% nominal operating-capital cost range. The denominator is not stripped of deposits or unproductive capex to improve optics. GQS 3.6 reflects weak demonstrated value growth, mixed profit sources and constrained incremental economics, not the absence of an addressable market.

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Saurabh and Sudarshan Saraogi bring long operating experience; the November rating describes more than 15 years. The September 2025 IPO raised ₹61.194 crore gross fresh cash, while ₹15.228 crore OFS proceeds belonged to sellers. Subsequent disclosed promoter purchases are secondary-market transactions, not fresh issuer funding. The 13:1 August 2024 bonus only capitalized reserves; fresh IPO shares, rather than the bonus, diluted proportional ownership. [S1,S2,S6,S20]

FY26 disclosed related-party rents total ₹6.517 crore and property-related security deposits ₹14.4498 crore, largely within total rental deposits ₹14.7396 crore. These are meaningful ongoing related-party economics requiring commercial scrutiny, not evidence that funds were diverted. AGM-approved FY27 rent ceilings sum to ₹9.16 crore; the S.L. Commercial ceiling ₹2.5 crore versus FY26 rent ₹0.24 crore motivates a ₹2.26 crore annual-cost sensitivity, not an assertion that the entire ceiling is payable. Approved salary-advance ceilings likewise are not automatic cash payments. Statutory and internal-control opinions are unmodified, and the auditor did not report fraud or current loan default. [S1,S14]

Promises versus delivery: the November 2025 target was Ahmedabad completion by March 2027; June 2026 investor notes moved operating expectations to Q1 FY28 and the annual report refers to FY28 operations, with land-registration resolution targeted H2 FY27. Only ₹0.20 crore monitored project use by June confirms early deployment, not finished capacity. Conversely, the new office was reported complete in April and backpack deliveries are a positive operating milestone. CFO Nitesh Agrawal resigned effective 6 June, stating a longer commute after relocation and no other material reason; Rajesh Kumar Jindal was appointed effective 16 August, after serving as GM operations since 2010. No resignation-related misconduct is inferred. [S1,S7,S9–S13]

At the 18 September AGM, management specifically described a global container shortage, higher freight costs and ready stock awaiting shipment, and warned of near-term margin pressure. It also claimed healthy FY26 volume growth continuing into Q1 FY27. These statements are attributed, not audited interim figures. The base therefore starts with an 8% core EBITDA margin, below FY26's 8.57%, before recovery to 9.5% and eventually 11%; it does not simply extrapolate a press-release profit-growth headline. Final shareholder approval of the three resolutions is confirmed by the 20 September results, not inferred from the proceedings alone. [S14,S21]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 profit before tax of ₹27.077 crore plus actual interest ₹2.5566 crore less other income ₹8.483 crore gives core EBIT ₹21.1506 crore. Adding depreciation ₹2.7037 crore gives core EBITDA ₹23.8543 crore. Bank charges of ₹0.4424 crore remain operating costs. FY25 restated core EBIT was ₹23.3548 crore, so normalized core EBIT fell 9.44% despite PAT increasing 7.24% on restated comparatives. Other income includes FX ₹4.4961 crore, interest ₹2.1646 crore and investment/trading gains ₹1.3936 crore. FX is economically connected to exports but volatile; a half-recurrence sensitivity avoids treating it as either permanently recurring or wholly irrelevant. Current-share PAT of ₹9.84 differs from reported weighted EPS of ₹11.00. [S1,S2,S4]

FY24–26 CFO of ₹20.0807/−4.9815/1.8071 crore totals ₹16.9063 crore, or 27.45% of restated PAT of ₹61.5964 crore. FY26 reported FCF after ₹12.4836 crore capex is −₹10.6765 crore. CFO includes ₹7.5 crore additional land advances and ₹11.7682 crore growth in rental security deposits, so weak cash is not solely weak customer collection. Those outlays still consume funds and are not erased to create free cash. Receivables fell, inventory rose ₹14.50 crore, and large deposits absorb capital. The original FY23 cash-flow statement reports ₹8.6736 crore CFO against the later IPO-restated ₹13.5586 crore; the restated stream is used and old classifications are not silently spliced. Original FY25 PAT of ₹18.8311 crore versus restated ₹18.8225 crore primarily reflects the disclosed gratuity correction. [S1–S5,S17]

The annual advances-note columns contain a presentation inconsistency: several amounts printed under FY26 match the original signed FY25 components. The signed current subtotal of ₹13.9873 crore reconciles. We preserve known net tax ₹0.2591 crore and capital advances ₹0.1695 crore separately, and classify the remaining ₹13.5587 crore as an operating-advances bundle without claiming an issuer-confirmed correction. A ₹3.6123 crore loss boundary tests the component ambiguity. This is not a finding of missing cash, and its bounded valuation effect does not justify suppressing all factors. Export C&F/CIF cutoff and disputed taxes are audit key matters with described procedures, not qualifications asserting overstatement. Bank stock-return differences, including ₹2.5848 crore in December and nil in March, are explained by the company as provisional cutoff, transit and overhead differences. [S1,S4,S5]

The 34-line claim ledger balances assets ₹247.0870 crore = equity ₹164.0868 crore + liabilities ₹83.0002 crore. Every tax credit, advance, interest, employee, statutory, expense, capital-creditor, debt, deposit and benefit claim has exactly one treatment. Bank debt of ₹59.6367 crore is on demand even where classified noncurrent; the ₹0.1371 crore vehicle balance amortizes separately. Opening capital creditors ₹2.8265 crore, accrued interest ₹0.0035 crore and current gratuity ₹0.1512 crore are explicitly paid. Noncurrent gratuity ₹0.857 crore and customer deposits ₹0.0009 crore remain terminal claims. Net current tax is not paid again gross. A ₹0.9701 crore disputed-tax call and ₹0.6247 crore guarantee call are downside assumptions; collateral is used first and no current-payment default is alleged. [S1,S4]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Entry equity value is ₹390.10 crore. Reported FY26 PAT implies 19.33× current-share earnings; the forward thesis cannot rely on that multiple without normalizing FX and investment income. Simple equity plus debt minus free cash is₹436.53 crore before separately identified realizable financial assets, about 20.64× current no-FX EBIT. Earmarked IPO deposits are not free surplus: their benefit enters through authorized project payments in the forecast. This avoids subtracting the same cash at entry and spending it again for free. [S1,S2,S15]

The base pays all scheduled claims and factory costs within the existing bank-debt envelope, reaches ₹416.49 crore revenue and ₹37.65 crore core EBIT, and applies 14× terminal EBIT. Terminal equity equals operating EV plus free cash minus bank debt and ₹0.8579 crore retained claims, with no separate addition of operating land, WC or rental deposits. Exit ₹262.24 implies6.64%IRR. Bear uses 9× EBIT, a 15% initial sales decline, 6–8% EBITDA margins, 75→60 debtor days and delayed project spending: exit ₹38.52, IRR −27.33%. Bull uses 18× EBIT, stronger growth and 10–13% margins: exit ₹552.12, IRR 23.76%. All three are financed without assumed rescue, but none is a forecast guarantee.

Base-value hurdle entries are₹148.80/₹130.38/₹114.63 for12%/15%/18%hurdles, before execution costs and investor tax. These conditional values are not target-price promises or recommended orders. At current entry, the 15% hurdle needs about 16.66% annual revenue growth, roughly ₹601 crore terminal sales with base margins and 14× EBIT. This is much higher than recent value growth and lacks independently verified volume support.

Single-variable tests remain below the 15% hurdle: half FY26 FX recurring gives 8.88% IRR; full book recovery of excluded investments 7.04%; minimum ₹50 crore project case 7.91%; 20% capex overrun 5.48%; extra ₹2.26 crore annual rent 4.96%. These do not establish a cheap hidden-asset case. A two-way growth/exit-multiple grid, funding gaps and 12/15/18% reverse solves are retained. No dividends are assumed; rescue equity, if separately explored, is issued at 60% of entry with 2% fees and fully dilutes shares.

Implementation check: the official 60-session window has 56 observations and four missing sessions, with no explicit zero-volume observations. Observed-only mean/median turnover is ₹50.41/₹27.59 lakh. A conservative missing-as-zero bound is ₹47.05/₹25.34 lakh; the latter gives 3.95 days for a ₹5 lakh exit at 5% participation, versus 9.87/1.97 days at 2%/10%. The 20-session window has 18 observations: observed-only mean/median ₹88.66/₹46.71 lakh, or conditional zero-filled ₹79.79/₹35.71 lakh. Missing observations are not asserted zero-trade days. The company was listed throughout the window. One 1,000-share lot costs ₹1,90,150; two lots are ₹3,80,300 and three ₹5,70,450, so an exact ₹5 lakh position is not implementable in whole lots. NSE's 19 October flags for fewer than 100 PANs and irregular trading apply on 21 October. There is no verified live spread/depth or guarantee of execution. [S15,S16]

The reverse 15% hurdle at the revised near-term margin assumptions needs about 16.66% annual revenue growth and ₹601 crore terminal sales, but peak bank funding is approximately ₹60.45 crore, ₹0.81 crore above the existing-draw envelope. That algebraic hurdle is not a funded forecast without additional verified financing or a changed cash policy. The 18% hurdle requires about 19.65% growth and ₹6.10 crore extra borrowing. A 30% bank-line withdrawal also breaks the base project schedule; this is a financing-failure alternative, not evidence that banks have withdrawn facilities or that optional growth must proceed regardless.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear argument is that capacity, stock and related-party property commitments grow before realizations and collections produce cash. Ecoline can remain a viable manufacturer while an investor overpays for incremental output. The ordinary funded bear loses about 80% of entry value. Halting optional Ahmedabad expansion improves the endpoint but still produces a negative shareholder return. Debt renewal and project profitability are separate questions. [S1,S2,S6]

Stress assumptions are tied to evidence rather than stacked to force failure: revenue contracted 10.37% in FY24; the top-ten buyer pool remains 57.80%; Acuité recorded debtor days rising from 43 to 63 when shipping routes changed, with inventory held for two to three months. A 15% sales decline, 75-day collections, 6% initial core EBITDA margin and modest 2% receivable/3% inventory write-down is the funded bear. The write-down lowers opening recoverable assets once; slower future collection affects new closing stocks, so the same bad receivable is not both written off and funded twice. No simultaneous tax or guarantee call is added to this credible bear.

A stronger 20% decline/90-day collection case halts optional expansion, retains restricted project cash of ₹49.8 crore, pays legacy claims and maintains operations. It needs ₹3.08 crore above the assumed ₹3 crore operating-cash buffer. With no required buffer, it survives within existing bank debt, with only about ₹0.03 crore first-year borrowing headroom. The buffer is not a legal obligation, so this near-edge case does not itself establish G3 Fail. At 105/120-day collections, shortfalls rise sharply; these are adverse boundaries beyond the observed 43–63-day history, not known current receivable ageing. Nearly all March 2026 net receivables were under six months old.

A 30% sales decline/120-day collection stack, including additional tax and collateral shocks, is an unfunded severe tail, not evidence of a present default. It receives no shareholder IRR without an explicit, dilutive rescue assumption. Current bank drawability, shipping routes and collection ageing could materially change the conditional G3 judgment. The surviving cases are retained alongside failure boundaries.

The September AGM container and freight warning provides a current operating reason to test shipping-delay stress, rather than treating it as a wholly remote historical analogy. Nevertheless, the company did not disclose a 105-day receivable average or a present bank withdrawal; those remain model boundaries, not observed facts. [S14]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A five-year 5× price outcome at the base 11% terminal core EBITDA margin and 14× EBIT requires roughly 39.78% annual revenue growth, ₹1,486 crore terminal revenue and ₹195.8 crore peak bank funding: about ₹136.2 crore beyond the modeled existing-debt envelope. A 10× outcome requires about 60.63% growth, ₹2,978 crore revenue and ₹508.9 crore peak bank funding, approximately ₹449.3 crore extra. These are algebraic demands, not funded price forecasts.

Dilutive equity, additional plants, customer acquisition, management capacity and new working capital would invalidate a naive unchanged-share extrapolation. Recent production and value history, together with the major project's early deployment, do not support either outcome. Even the bull case is about 2.9×, conditional on substantially stronger execution.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Track actual Ahmedabad land registration against H2 FY27 and physical commissioning against FY28, not only allocation announcements. Revised dates or costs require a fresh funding model.
2. Reconcile monitored project spending from ₹0.20 crore at June, remaining IPO objects and bank deposits. Cash released for one purpose must not be assumed usable for another.
3. Demand a value, volume and realization bridge. FY26 revenue was ₹278.40 crore and both halves were approximately ₹139.2 crore. Check whether higher units restore core profit rather than only total income.
4. Track core EBITDA margin of 8.57%, excluding other income, alongside a separate FX bridge. The modeled 11% margin must be earned through utilization and integration.
5. Track reported CFO/PAT of 27.45% over FY24–26, receivable ageing, inventory of ₹61.33 crore and ordinary advances of ₹13.56 crore. Collections approaching 90 days alongside sales and margin pressure are a funding warning, not automatically a default.
6. Verify demand-bank renewals, actual available headroom and cash restrictions. The ₹8.5 crore nonfund rating is not cash. Update legacy creditor and benefit settlements.
7. Track actual related-party property rents and deposits against ₹6.517 crore and ₹14.4498 crore, respectively, and approved ceilings. Obtain commercial benchmarks rather than assuming approval establishes fairness.
8. Recheck tax-appeal outcomes, cutoff controls and advances-note presentation in the next signed report. This checklist does not create automatic monitoring or outreach.
9. Before any implementation, recheck the 1,000-share lot, spreads, depth, circuit or auction conditions and surveillance for the actual position size. Historical turnover does not guarantee an exit.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
BQS 4.52 and IAS 3.33 place Ecoline in Weak setup / value-trap risk under the framework matrix. GQS 3.60 does not meet the compounder criteria. The appropriate archetype is an execution-dependent manufacturing expansion with commodity and FX exposure. This is not Avoid — governance and not an actual distress or default declaration. G3 remains Conditional because funded countercases exist and the near-edge case can remove its discretionary cash buffer without rescue.

Conditional action: research watchlist only at the stated price, with no purchase or trade instructed by this model. The approximate ₹114.63–148.80 base-value entry range corresponds to 18–12% hurdles, with ₹130.38 at 15%; a lower price does not cure weak cash or project risk. A stronger entry case requires verified project progress, core earnings and cash improvement, and updated bank liquidity.

If credible essential-operation stress develops an unfinanceable shortfall after haltable growth is stopped, G3 must change to Fail and IAS be capped at 3. The current surviving case cannot be ignored. This assessment is conditional on a theoretical ₹5 lakh liquidity reference, not user-specific suitability.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The primary base is the FY2026 annual report and signed results, September 2025 prospectus with restated financials, original FY2022–25 accounts, March and June IPO monitoring, recent operating/CFO/AGM filings, and official NSE market files. Acuité's November 2025 rationale provides an independent credit and working-capital cross-check, but does not verify October 2026 facility availability. The old rating PDF returned 404; its published HTML rationale was read. Company-presentation market-size estimates are not independently verified and are not valuation inputs. Sources are claim-linked rather than decorative authority.

Open questions are bounded and consequential: confirm the detailed advances-column labels; reconcile IPO objects against bank earmarks and fees; identify which old CWIP belongs to which site; update original capex quotes and land obligations; verify current facility renewal and unrestricted cash; and obtain clean unit-price growth and related-property benchmarks. Original FY21 cash-flow and FY23 presentation differences lower historical comparability confidence but do not override current signed claims. The current tax asset is net, with no repeated gross liability. Deferred tax, illiquid investments, collateral and unspent project reserves are not free cash.

All scenario inputs are analyst assumptions, not issuer accounts or forecasts. March opening stocks plus only known June IPO uses are a proxy, not October balance-sheet verification. No options, warrants or new acquisition perimeter were identified in the checked filings. Actual issued shares are used, and modeled rescue explicitly dilutes them. Returns are nominal and pretax, excluding execution costs. Scoring thresholds organize judgment; they are not statistically validated return or default predictors.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audit and disclosed uses are positive; large promoter-property rents and deposits and imperfect note comparatives limit stewardship confidence. No abuse or fraud is alleged.

MOAT.reason: Useful customer relationships, certifications and multiple locations remain contestable; manufacturing and procurement are competitive and buyer concentration matters.

REV.reason: Selected FY23–26 CAGR of −2.8536% starts at 1. Add one point for corroborated realization decline: packaging output rose from 62.447m to 65.029m pieces in FY23–25 while value fell. This is not complete volume proof. No additional trajectory bonus; the COVID-base CAGR is not selected.

DUR.reason: Reusable bags, new capacity and backpack access provide runway, constrained by short orders, land/commissioning risk and customer concentration.

CAP.reason: Current no-FX NOPAT divided by operating capital is approximately 11.47%, not clear excess over a 12–15% capital-cost range. New-factory returns are unproven; no clean aggregate incremental ROIC is fabricated.

CASH.reason: Three-year reported conversion of 27.45% and two weak recent years are material. Land and rental-deposit investment and strong FY24 cash temper a persistent-collection-failure verdict. Score 4 does not trigger a GQS cap.

BAL.reason: Base and 15%/75-day bear are funded without a new facility. The 20%/90-day restrained case survives only by nearly exhausting cash. Restricted IPO deposits and demand debt create material stress sensitivity.

EXEC.reason: New leased capacity and backpack deliveries are observable. Ahmedabad moved from March 2027 to FY28; only ₹0.2 crore was deployed by June. Recent half-year revenue is flat and PAT lower.

EARN.reason: PAT growth depends on FX, investment and interest income while normalized EBIT declined. Fresh shares mean current-share PAT of ₹9.84 is below weighted EPS of ₹11.00.

R.reason: The 6.64% base IRR less the 15% hurdle falls in the −10 to −7 percentage-point band. Historical source confidence is not forecast certainty.

D.reason: The funded bear loses about 80% of entry value. Collection-stress survival is thin and severe tails need rescue. This is shareholder impairment risk, not an actual default allegation.

P.reason: The 15% hurdle requires about 16.5% revenue CAGR, an 11% terminal EBITDA margin and 14× EBIT, substantially above recent value growth. Several optimistic assumptions must coincide.

L.reason: Conditional conservative turnover implies 3.95 days at 5% participation, starting at 7. Deduct one point for the 1,000-share lot, missing observations and thin-activity flags. Live depth is unverified.

Q.reason: Reuse final unrounded BQS once, without a separate GQS or ROIC premium.

monitoring_plan:
1. Track actual Ahmedabad land registration against H2 FY27 and physical commissioning against FY28, not only allocation announcements. Revised dates or costs require a fresh funding model.
2. Reconcile monitored project spending from ₹0.20 crore at June, remaining IPO objects and bank deposits. Cash released for one purpose must not be assumed usable for another.
3. Demand a value, volume and realization bridge. FY26 revenue was ₹278.40 crore and both halves were approximately ₹139.2 crore. Check whether higher units restore core profit rather than only total income.
4. Track core EBITDA margin of 8.57%, excluding other income, alongside a separate FX bridge. The modeled 11% margin must be earned through utilization and integration.
5. Track reported CFO/PAT of 27.45% over FY24–26, receivable ageing, inventory of ₹61.33 crore and ordinary advances of ₹13.56 crore. Collections approaching 90 days alongside sales and margin pressure are a funding warning, not automatically a default.
6. Verify demand-bank renewals, actual available headroom and cash restrictions. The ₹8.5 crore nonfund rating is not cash. Update legacy creditor and benefit settlements.
7. Track actual related-party property rents and deposits against ₹6.517 crore and ₹14.4498 crore, respectively, and approved ceilings. Obtain commercial benchmarks rather than assuming approval establishes fairness.
8. Recheck tax-appeal outcomes, cutoff controls and advances-note presentation in the next signed report. This checklist does not create automatic monitoring or outreach.
9. Before any implementation, recheck the 1,000-share lot, spreads, depth, circuit or auction conditions and surveillance for the actual position size. Historical turnover does not guarantee an exit.
limitations: October cash and bank availability are not independently verified; the model uses audited March stocks and only known June IPO uses.
Detailed advances-column labels require issuer confirmation; the subtotal and known tax/capital claims are verified and a bounded loss variant is provided.
Project cost, timing, land commitments and old CWIP allocation need updates. New-factory returns remain unproven.
Older FY21/FY23 cash-flow presentation and restatements reduce historical comparability; the latest restated FY23–25 stream is explicitly chosen.
Valuation depends on growth, margin, exit and demand-debt renewal assumptions. Unfunded paths are not investable returns.
Live spreads and depth are unknown. Missing historical observations are conditionally zero-filled only as a conservative bound, not asserted zero-trade sessions.
